message.text: The new bound is tested for named triage only, not for named early lens copies. All early-copy tests use a single unnamed copy, so they do not establish that named early copies consume the extras budget.

explanation.what: The new bound is tested for named triage only, not for named early lens copies. All early-copy tests use a single unnamed copy, so they do not establish that named early copies consume the extras budget.
explanation.whatToDo: Add a boundary test with 64 and 65 distinct early lens records named by the round (and a valid account), asserting acceptance at 64 and tooManyExtras at 65.
explanation.whyHere: This change explicitly removes the named-record exemption for early lens copies too. Restoring that exemption only for lens records would leave the new tests passing while allowing more than 64 extras.

properties.failureScenario: Mutate the loop to continue when read.has(record.id) && record.kind === 'lens', before testing extra(record). A valid writer batch with a check, its account, 65 distinct no-check lens records, and a round reading them all is then accepted instead of refused with tooManyExtras. The named-triage boundary test still fails appropriately at 65 triages, and the existing early-copy tests only exercise unnamed single copies, so none catches this mutation.
